claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you asking about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm asking about my one child - Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

To help determine your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

**First, is Alex your biological child, adopted child, or a child you're a foster parent or guardian for?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Next, how old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you providing that information.

**Is Alex in paid work or self-employment?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that confirmation.

**Do you currently live in the UK, and have you lived here for the past two years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and have been here for years.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

**Finally, are you or anyone else already claiming Child Benefit for Alex with another government agency or local authority?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have what I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, let me evaluate your situation against the Child Benefit eligibility rules:

- Alex is your biological child
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex is not in full-time education or an approved training scheme
- Alex is not in paid work
- You are a British citizen
- You live in the UK and have been here for years
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Unfortunately, **Child Benefit is only payable for children up to age 16, or up to age 19 if they are in full-time education or an approved training scheme**. Since Alex is 16 and not in full-time education or an approved training scheme, he no longer qualifies for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. While you meet the residency and citizenship requirements, Alex's age and current circumstances mean he falls outside the eligible age range for Child Benefit.

If Alex were to enter full-time education or training in the future, the situation could change, and you might become eligible again. You may want to get in touch with HMRC if Alex's circumstances change.
